CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Steve Talt, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 8, 2024, AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Talt, Vice Mayor Shepherd
Romey, and Mayor Huang

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

  NEW BUSINESS

 1.  AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL DESIGN SERVICES AGREEMENT TO NV5
  FOR PREPARATION OF PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS, AND COST
  ESTIMATES FOR THE FY 2023-24 ALLEY AND PARKING LOT
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM PROJECT NO. 23-0532 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $64,930

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council award a Professional
  Services Agreement to NV5 in the amount of $64,930 to prepare design plans,
  specifications, and cost estimates for the FY 2023-24 Alley and Parking Lot
  Improvement Program Project. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to award a Professional Services Agreement to NV5 for design services
  including the preparation of plans, specifications and cost estimates for the Fiscal
  Year 2023-24 Alley and Parking Lot Improvement Program Project No. 23-0532 in an
  amount not to exceed $64,930 and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement on behalf of the City.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 2.  AWARD OF BUS TRANSPORTATION SERVICES AGREEEMENT TO
  MISSION SCHOOL TRANSPORTATION, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $42,500

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council award the bus transportation
  services agreement to Mission School Transportation, Inc. If the City Council concurs
  with Staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to award a Vendor Agreement to Mission School Transportation, Inc., in the
  amount of $42,500 for youth related bus transportation services, with the City
  Manager being authorized to execute the agreement on behalf of the City, as well as
  four one-year contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.”

AGENDA – MAY 08, 2024  PAGE 3 of 7
  3.  APPROVAL OF PROCUREMENT OF NEW INTEGRATED LIBRARY SYSTEM
  SOFTWARE WITH A YEAR 1 CONTRACT AMOUNT OF $11,900

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve of the procurement of new
  Integrated Library System software, Apollo by Biblionix, for the Community Services
  Department, Library Division. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve of the procurement of new Integrated Library System software,
  Apollo by Biblionix, for the Community Services Department, Library Division with a
  total Year 1 cost of $11,900, with the City Manager being authorized to execute the
  agreement on behalf of the City, and authorize the City Manager to approve annual
  renewals, subject to satisfactory service and Council budget allocation.”

 4.  APPROVAL OF AN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN MARINO
  AND INTIME CLOUD HOSTED SCHEDULING SOFTWARE AND
  WORKFORCE MANAGEMENT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council authorize and direct the City
  Manager to enter into an agreement with InTime Solutions for cloud hosted
  scheduling and workforce management software. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with InTime
  Solutions for cloud hosted scheduling and workforce management software, and to
  appropriate $11,360 from COPS Fund reserves to account 233-30-4150-0500 (Other
  Contract Services IT).”

 5.  MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL
  OF GOVERNMENTS TO PAY ADDITIONAL COST SHARE OBLIGATIONS
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $8,954.60 FOR PARTICIPATION IN 2018-2023
  STORMWATER  QUALITY  IMPROVEMENT  AND  MONITORING
  PROGRAMS FOR LOS ANGELES RIVER

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the Memorandum of
  Agreement for the Upper Los Angeles River Watershed Management Area. If Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Memorandum of Agreement with San Gabriel Valley Council
  of Governments regarding administration and additional cost sharing obligations in
  the amount of $8,954.60 for implementing the 2018-2023 Coordinated Integrated
  Monitoring Program (CIMP) and Watershed Management Program (WMP) for the
  Upper Los Angeles River Watershed Management Area.”

 6.  APPROVAL OF NOVATION AGREEMENT TRANSFERRING EXISTING
  CONTRACT  RESPONSIBILITIES  OF  COLUMBIA
  TELECOMMUNICATIONS CORPORATION TO IMPERIAL COUNTY
  OFFICE OF EDUCATION FOR THE PROVISION, INSTALLATION, AND
  MAINTENANCE OF ADVANCED NETWORK SERVICES AT THE CROWELL
  PUBLIC LIBRARY

AGENDA – MAY 08, 2024  PAGE 4 of 7
   Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the novation agreement
  with Imperial County Office of Education transferring existing contract responsibilities
  from Columbia Telecommunications Corporation for the provision, installation, and
  maintenance of advanced network services at the Crowell Public Library. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the novation agreement with Imperial County Office of Education
  transferring existing contract responsibilities from Columbia Telecommunications
  Corporation for the provision, installation, and maintenance of advanced network
  services, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on behalf of the
  City.”

 7.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-07, A REVIEW OF THE SAN
  MARINO POLICE DEPARTMENT MILITARY EQUIPMENT ANNUAL
  REPORT AND RENEWAL OF SAN MARINO CITY ORDINANCE O-22-
  1390 AND SAN MARINO POLICE DEPARTMENT POLICY 705

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution No. R-24-07,
  renewing both San Marino City Ordinance No. O-22-1390 and San Marino Police
  Department Policy 705, and finding that the San Marino Police Department Military
  Equipment Annual Report complies with the standards of approval set forth in
  Government Code § 7070, 7071 and 7072. If the City Council agrees with staff’s
  recommendation an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-24-07: a review of the San Marino Police
  Department Military Equipment Annual Report and Renewal of San Marino City
  Ordinance No. O-22-1390 and San Marino Police Department Policy 705.”

 8.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R-24-06, ADOPTING A LIST OF
  STREET PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 FUNDED BY SB1, THE
  ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Resolution No. R-24-
  06, adopting a list of street projects for Fiscal Year 2024-25 funded by SB1. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Resolution No. R-24-06 adopting a list of Fiscal Year 2024-25
  projects to be funded by SB1 Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account Funds.”

 9.  SIDE LETTER OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE SAN MARINO POLICE
  OFFICERS ASSOCIATION (“SMPOA”) AND THE CITY OF SAN MARINO
  (“CITY”) CONCERNING EXPANDING THE CATASTROPHIC LEAVE
  PROGRAM

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt the Side Letter of Agreement
  between the San Marino Police Officers Association (“SMPOA”) and the City of San
  Marino (“City”).

  “I move to adopt the Side Letter of Agreement between the San Marino Police

   Officers Association (“SMPOA”) and the City of San Marino (“City”) concerning
  expanding the Catastrophic Leave Program.”

 10. APPROVAL OF NOTICE OF COMPLETION FOR YEAR 2 OF THE ANNUAL
  SIDEWALK REPLACEMENT PROGRAM PROJECT NO. 23-9272

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council accept Year 2 of the
  Multi-Year Sidewalk Replacement Program as complete and authorize the City Clerk
  to file the Notice of Completion. If the City Council concurs, an appropriate motion
  would be:

  “I move to accept Year 2 of the Multi-Year Sidewalk Replacement Program Project
  No. 23-9272 performed by CJ Concrete Construction, Inc., as complete, and
  authorize the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion.”

 11. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF MARCH 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of March
  2024.”

 12. RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR APRIL
  2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of April 2024. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of April
  2024.”

 13. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the April 2024 minutes. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of April 10, 2024, the regular
  meeting of April 10, 2024, the adjourned regular meeting of April 26, 2024, and the
  special meeting of April 26, 2024.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
